newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex bond bumped up on strong investor demand.
newsitem.headline: Pemex bond bumped up on strong investor demand.

text.p: Strong demand for the latest Eurobond from Petroleos Mexicanos caused the state-owned oil company to increase its size to $300 million from the originally planned $250 million, sources said on Monday.
"It was very well received. There was a lot of appetite for the paper," said the source, who was close to the deal.
"Basically with the size of demand for the paper it made sense to increase the amount," the source, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
The five-year issue was led by Swiss Bank Corp and Goldman Sachs. The issue was pre-marketed on Friday and placed on Monday. Swiss Bank was the bookrunner on the issue.
Although the issue was aimed initially at the retail market in Europe, it also garnered good interest from institutional investors. The issue also saw strong interest from investors in Asia.
The state-owned oil company was also able to lower its borrowing costs with its latest Eurobond.
The latest bond had an 8.0 percent coupon and was placed at 160 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
That compares with a spread of 175 basis points over U.S. Treasuries on Pemex's last Eurobond, a $300 million three-year Eurobond placed last October.
Pemex has a strategy of extending the maturity of its debt, moving toward the medium-term issues from the two- and three-year issues it placed in 1996.
The company's paper normally receives a warm welcome from investors, for its rarity value and the premium investors give to Latin American oil-producers, analysts said.
Earlier this year, company officials said it planned to place about $800 million in debt this year.
The first issue this year was a 350 million Italian lira seven-year Eurobond, worth the equivalent of $207 million. That was placed in March.
Pemex placed three bonds worth about $800 million in 1996. It will have $1.2 billion in maturing debt in 1997.
